## Selection Criteria for Pork Processing
1. Cleanability - Material must withstand CIP (Clean-in-Place) with alkaline/acid detergents without degradation. Surface roughness Ra < 32 μin recommended.
2. Chemical Resistance - Contact with sanitizers (quaternary ammonium, peracetic acid), blood proteins, and pork fats. Request compatibility charts from gasket vendor.

3. Temperature Rating - Consider steam sterilization (250°F/121°C peak) and refrigeration zones. EPDM gaskets rated to 400°F but not oil-resistant; Viton better for fat contact.
4. Reuse Frequency - Sanitary flange gaskets (tri-clamp style) typically replaced each disassembly. UHMW works well for static seals; replace PTFE if compressed set exceeds 15%.

jina.title: Resistant starch – the secret to enjoying white carbs without feeling guilty - NatureDoc
jina.snippet:
**We are often told that potatoes, pasta and rice are the demon white carbs that we need to cut back on if we want to avoid piling on the pounds or preventing a bloated tummy. But look closer and you will find that they can actually help balance your appetite and improve digestion if you eat them in the most optimal way.**

**The secret is in increasing the levels of resistant starch found in these foods.**

### Get our lovely Healthy Bites newsletter!

Each week, you’ll get an amazing recipe, a useful health tip, and an ingredient to jazz up your shopping basket!

## What is the difference between starch and resistant starch?

You are probably aware that starches are complex carbohydrates that are broken down into glucose and absorbed into the bloodstream from our small intestine. On the other hand, resistant starches are carbohydrates which are not digested or broken down and remain in the gut. They are therefore considered a fibre. Resistant starch also plays an important role in providing food for the good bacteria in our gut which in turn bolsters the diversity in the gut microbiome.

The biggest source of resistant starch is in green unripe bananas. I wouldn’t recommend eating these raw but you can buy green banana flour and pasta in some health food shops. Even eating harder and less ripe bananas is better than eating the sweeter riper ones in terms of levels of resistant starch and helpful fibre.

Beans, chickpeas and lentils are also a good choice for resistant starch. These are easy to add to the diet through eating hummus or dhal, or by adding a tin of beans or lentils to pies, soup or casseroles.

Not many people realise that foods like potatoes, pasta and rice have high levels of starch when hot, but are great sources of resistant starch when they are cold.

This is because the starch changes its structure when it’s heated and cooled, morphing from the digestible starch we associate with these high carb foods to the beneficial fibrous resistant starch.

## Food Grade Gasket Materials: Why Specification Matters

## **In food and beverage processing, the margin for error is non-existent. A single component failure doesn’t just mean downtime; it can mean product contamination, costly recalls, and significant reputational damage.**

While they are often physically small components, gaskets play a critical role in maintaining the integrity of hygienic processing lines.

Choosing the correct material for a food-grade gasket is not simply a matter of finding something that fits the flange. It is a precise engineering decision that requires balancing chemical compatibility, temperature resistance, and regulatory compliance.

**The Critical Importance of Material Selection**

Every gasket starts with choosing the right material. This step is critical to performance, particularly in the food industry where ‘food safe’ is a broad term that covers various regulatory standards and physical properties.

The primary function of any gasket is to create a seal that prevents leakage. However, in food applications, the gasket must also:

1. **Resist degradation:** It must withstand the specific food products being processed (acids, fats, oils) and the harsh chemicals used in Clean-in-Place (CIP) procedures.
1. **Prevent contamination:** The material must not leach harmful substances into the product (migration) or affect the taste/odour of the food (organoleptic properties).
1. **Inhibit bacterial growth:** The surface must be non-porous and resistant to bacterial colonisation.

If a buyer specifies a generic “rubber gasket” without considering these factors, the result can be premature failure. For example, using a standard EPDM gasket in a line processing vegetable oils will result in the seal swelling and disintegrating, as standard EPDM is not compatible with fats and oils.

Silicone rubber is a gasket material that’s versatile to many industries, from medical to food-processing. Typically used in marine and other outdoor applications, neoprene rubber has the ability to resist moderate levels of sunlight, ozone, and other weather elements along with greases, fats, and oils.
It’s a popular choice for a reason — natural rubber is a good all-around, general-purpose gasket material. While it shouldn’t be used with fuels, oils or solvents, natural rubber is incredibly water resistant and works very well with metal surfaces.
Natural rubber is great to use with water pumps and pipes for its good shock and vibration resistance qualities. Natural gum rubber is a gasket material that makes great insulation for water pumps and pipes.
